name: Carpenter’s Gap ground-edge axe production
description: A basalt flake with an abraded bevel is interpreted as removal from a ground-edge axe, documenting a method for making and resharpening cutting edges.

date.label: Approximately 49,000–44,000 cal BP
date.basis: Authors associate the axe flake with a charcoal sample in the same excavation unit, dated 48,875–43,941 calibrated BP; rounded BCE endpoints use 1950 as reference.

events.statement: The flake and associated charcoal in excavation unit 52 provide evidence of ground-edge axe working.

evidence.supports: The flake and associated charcoal in excavation unit 52 provide evidence of ground-edge axe working.

contributions.resource: Ground and flaked stone cutting edges

evidence.supports: The source describes Aboriginal toolmakers at Carpenter’s Gap 1 and this contribution.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest sourced date for the specific documented case; this does not establish invention or worldwide priority.

caveats: Charcoal is contextually associated rather than a direct date on the stone; movement and axe identification are archaeological interpretations. The rounded range is not global priority.

research.note: Independently checked the reported specimen and dated associated charcoal against Hiscock et al.; attribution of the flake to a ground axe and stratigraphic association remain interpretations.
